description:
## Corrected count: 30, not 42

The original 42 came from a scan that looked for 'pub fn' per file without checking whether the DECLARING MODULE is gated. A pub fn inside a #[cfg(test)] mod is already invisible to production. Excluding gated modules -- fixture_facts.rs, telemetry/capture.rs, telemetry/public_trace.rs and 43 *_test.rs files -- the true count is 30.

That is what put events, events_named, count_by_kind, spans_named and the fixture_facts pair on the original list. They were never in scope.

## They are two populations, not one

Public front-door API, where no in-repo production caller is EXPECTED and gating would be wrong:
  Compiler2::set_output (only caller is public_trace.rs, itself gated)
  Compiler2::compile_root_jit, Compiler2::retire_root_products -- see fz-foq.5
  parser::lexer::tokenize, source_map::add_code, diagnostic::with_secondary

Internal accessors that leaked pub and should be cfg(test) or pub(crate):
  world::callsite_targets, callsite_target_resolution, code_surface
  deps::waiters, facts::satisfies, scheduler::settle_quiescent_ordered
  module_interface::exported_functions, exported_macros, macro_with_name_arity
  types/addressed::address_arrow, param_alpha_id, result_alpha_id
  quoted_surface::read_compiler_fragment_surface

The causal.rs entries (metadata_key, parse_public_trace, canonical_multiset, derive_requests, formula_totals, product_totals, functions) are held by fz-0am: much of that module is scheduled to stop existing, so classify them after that arc, not before.

## Mechanic

For the leaked internals: move into a #[cfg(test)] impl block on the owning type. They are methods, not free functions, so they cannot literally move into a test file. cfg(test) beats pub(crate) -- the item does not exist in a production build, so reuse is a compile error rather than a judgment call, and cfg(test) items stay visible to unit tests across modules.

For the API population: leave them, and record WHY in one place so the next scan does not re-raise them.

Done when every fully-pub function is either called from production, deliberately named as API, or behind cfg(test).
title: Sort the 30 test-only pub functions into API and leaked internals
